clue.text: Scowl is preceded by liquid company with time for an artist

indicators.note: the scowl-and-is pair comes after the liquid and company, so those are placed in front

parts.note: water is the commonest liquid
to lour (or lower) is to scowl or frown

explanation.surface: A painter is pictured joining a firm of liquid suppliers, scowling all the while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is preceded by' sets the liquid and company in front of the scowl; LOUR is an old verb for frowning darkly.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter who works in water-based paints is one kind of artist.

clue.text: A rewritten piece may make it clear

indicators.note: something rewritten has its contents put down again in a new order, so the letters of the last two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Redrafting a newspaper story may make its meaning plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' signals rearranging IT CLEAR; 'A' and 'may make' are link words, though the surface also hints that the answer, rewritten, gives 'it clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper or magazine item is called a piece or an article.

clue.text: Secret subjects for a girl on twinkling toes

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits below it, so the girl follows
twinkling toes move quickly about, so the letters of toes are jumbled

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A dancer called Erica studies arcane matters on her nimble feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twinkling' turns TOES into ESOT, and 'on' in a down answer places ERICA beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric matters are obscure knowledge understood only by an inner circle, hence secret subjects.

clue.text: Feline relatives are something of botanical interest

parts.note: a feline is a cat
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A cat's family members are said to fascinate botanists.
explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is the dangling flower spike of trees such as hazel and willow, a botanical feature.

clue.text: Make-up gives sign of approval to features

parts.note: the lips are among the facial features
a tick marks something as correct or approved

explanation.surface: A cosmetic product earns a mark of approval for one's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives ... to' simply joins the two pieces: the tick is given to the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip colouring is a staple cosmetic, so it is a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Strip the chaos of ruin with gravity

indicators.note: the chaos of the word ruin means its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Someone strips away the wreckage of a ruin with all due seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos of' rearranges RUIN to UNRI, then G is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip it of its rigging, so the verb means strip.

clue.text: Make progress, making the little devil wander off

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
to rove is to wander or roam

explanation.surface: Getting better means letting the mischievous imp go roaming away.
explanation.definitionFit: To get better is to advance, which is making progress.

clue.text: Ragged fellow badly tattered with female feline tail

indicators.note: the feline goes at the tail end of the answer
badly signals that the letters of the following words are put together wrongly

parts.note: ma, a mother, is a female
the lion is the great feline

explanation.surface: A scruffy man is described in torn clothes alongside a female cat's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TATTERED plus MA into TATTERDEMA; 'tail' puts LION at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatterdemalion is a person dressed in rags, a ragged fellow or scarecrow figure.

clue.text: Frustration of a girl needing a job

parts.note: a girl's is DI'S, with Di as the girl's name and the possessive giving S
an appointment is a post or job

explanation.surface: A young woman's annoyance at needing employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointment is the feeling of hopes being let down, close to frustration.

clue.text: Something musical in a bird without alternative backing

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the bird surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: backing means the word for alternative runs backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Some music is said to lie inside a bird lacking a fallback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'backing' turns the alternative round before the bird encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or chant sung at the start of a church service, a piece of music.

clue.text: Wall provided a role with mimic in it

indicators.note: in shows the mimic placed inside the role

parts.note: an actor's part is their role
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: An actor gets a wall-climbing role provided they can do impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided a' and 'it' only join; 'Wall' looks like a verb but is the plain noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along a roof, bridge or balcony edge.

clue.text: His hope to discover elixir of life disturbs St Michael?

definitions.text: His hope to discover elixir of life

indicators.note: disturbing the saint's name throws its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's quest for the potion of eternal life troubles the archangel Michael.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbs' rearranges ST MICHAEL; the definition describes the man rather than giving a synonym, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners of this pseudo-science sought the elixir of life and the philosopher's stone.

clue.text: Writer on music for the wood

definitions.meaning: Sir George ... compiled the famous Dictionary of Music and Musicians
a small wood or group of trees

explanation.definitionFit: Grove's Dictionary of Music is named after its editor, and a grove is a small stand of trees, a little wood.

clue.text: Bird when small goes back in hole

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground

indicators.note: goes back means the word for small is read in reverse

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A small bird retreats into its hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns the Scots word for small around, and 'in' lodges it inside the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is another name for the lapwing, named for its call.

clue.text: Reserve if backing age in a very inhospitable place

parts.note: ice means reserve or coldness of manner

indicators.note: backing means the little word if is turned round

parts.note: eld is an old word for age

explanation.surface: Someone's reserves are depleted, retreating in old age to a harsh place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the little word round; ELD is an archaic word for old age that setters often use.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice field is a vast sheet of ice, about as hostile to life as anywhere.

clue.text: Michael's device as a piece of furniture

parts.note: Michael Foot was leader of the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983, and the possessive gives S
a tool is a device

explanation.surface: A politician's gadget turns out to be furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot was a well-known British Labour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A low stool for resting the feet is an item of furniture.

clue.text: Stir and boil varied cones

indicators.note: varied means the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to stir and boil some pine cones in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges STIR and BOIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobili are the cone-shaped fruiting bodies of conifers and some other plants.

clue.text: Moments when saints are confused about part of Bible

indicators.note: about here means around, so the scrambled saints surround the Bible part
saints being confused have their letters put in disorder

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, one part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Short periods when holy people get muddled over scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are confused' scrambles the holy people, and 'about' wraps them round the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Instants are very brief spells of time, synonyms for moments.

clue.text: Staying power for beginning of a leader about a leader

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Staying power for beginning of a leader about a leader': ST(AMIN)A needs STA, which 'beginning of a leader' cannot give; likely misprinted and not found online.
annotationWithheld.clue: Staying power for beginning of a leader about a leader

clue.text: Animal churning up moss

indicators.note: churning stirs violently, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A creature churns up some moss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning' rearranges UP MOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A possum is a marsupial mammal of Australia or America, an animal.

clue.text: Races converted into priests

indicators.note: something converted is made over into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Whole ethnic groups are turned into clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted into' rearranges PRIESTS; read the other way, the answer rearranged gives priests.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirpes are lines of descent or stocks, the sense of races as lineages.

clue.text: Time for car?

parts.note: a dog is said to be in this state when on heat, and the word also means a period of the year

explanation.walkthrough: A bitch on heat is 'in season', so the period is a time for a cur; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of the year, and also the breeding time of an animal.

clue.text: Not seen in London, they are the reverse of fashionable

indicators.note: the reverse of means the word for fashionable is read backwards

parts.note: smart means stylish or fashionable

explanation.surface: Vehicles missing from London streets are deemed hopelessly out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: When the puzzle appeared London had scrapped its street trams, which only returned with Croydon Tramlink in 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: Street railway cars had vanished from London, so these vehicles were not seen there.

clue.text: Japanese wall is rising about almost burning Japan

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the rest
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something burning is hot
J is the international vehicle code for Japan

explanation.surface: A Japanese partition goes up around the nearly blazing country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the little word upwards, 'almost' docks the heat word's last letter, and 'about' wraps one round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoji is a sliding paper screen used as a wall or partition in Japanese houses.

clue.text: Cricket ball makes surplus population

parts.note: overs are the sets of six balls bowled in cricket
pill is slang for a ball

explanation.surface: A cricket ball creates an excess of people.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is people moved out of an overcrowded city into new towns, surplus population.

clue.text: I depart after a letter from Northern Ireland calls for descendants

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'I depart after a letter from Northern Ireland calls for descendants': EP + I GO + NI needs EP, which 'a letter' does not give; likely misprinted.
annotationWithheld.clue: I depart after a letter from Northern Ireland calls for descendants

clue.text: Poor Cis is involved with group of stars

indicators.note: being involved means tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poorly girl named Cis gets mixed up with astrology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved' rearranges POOR CIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is a constellation, the Scorpion, a group of stars.

clue.text: Lover of the past, I shoot back with weight about me on a file

indicators.note: back means the word for shoot is reversed

parts.note: to dart is to shoot forward

indicators.note: about means the weight goes around the speaker

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
me is the speaker, I
a list is a file or roll

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person aims backwards, burdened, on a ranked roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the verb for shoot round, 'about' wraps the weight round the speaker, and 'on' joins the final pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditionalist clings to customs and ways of earlier times.
